title: Software Engineer, Product Velocity
description:
About the Team

The ChatGPT Velocity team owns the health of the end-to-end developer and deploy loop for ChatGPT-facing services. Our mission is to help ChatGPT engineers ship confidently with a fast, lightweight development cycle and a trusted path to production.

ChatGPT development depends on a long chain: local environments, Bazel builds, CI, tests, merges, release candidates, deploys, synthetics, alerts, and production health. When any link is slow, flaky, or unclear, engineers lose hours, fixes reach users later, and on-call load rises. This team turns that cross-cutting drag into owned, measured, and durable improvements.

About the Role

We are hiring an experienced infrastructure engineer to make ChatGPT development dramatically faster and more reliable. You will work across local development, build systems, CI, deployment infrastructure, test ownership, and production safety signals to reduce the time and attention required to move a healthy change from development to production.

This is not a narrow tooling role. The best person for this job will be comfortable diagnosing messy distributed systems, reading developer pain signals from Slack and metrics, building reliable automation, negotiating ownership across teams, and making tradeoffs between velocity and production safety. You should enjoy treating engineers as users and turning confusing workflow failures into clear, measured systems.

In this role, you will:

 - Reduce local development startup and iteration latency for ChatGPT engineers

 - Improve Bazel and build performance for local machines, devboxes, and CI, including cache effectiveness, reproducibility, disk usage, remote cache behavior, and observability into invalidations.

 - Improve CI reliability and merge throughput by reducing unrelated failures, tail latency, flaky or mis-owned tests, quarantine friction, and repeated manual reruns.

 - Build agents that help PRs make forward progress: rebasing, conflict resolution, CI triage, safe reruns, owner routing, and clear identification of external blockers.

 - Make deploy pipelines more self-healing, especially when transient alerts, known-bad clusters, recovered synthetics, stale RCs, or noisy gates should not require human babysitting.

 - Improve deploy observability so engineers can quickly tell where a change is, what is blocking it, whether the signal is trustworthy, and who owns the next action.

 - Establish lightweight metrics for before-and-after impact, such as commit-to-prod latency, deploy-window throughput, CI tail latency, local bootup time, failure rates, manual interventions, false-positive gates, and developer-reported pain.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong experience with large-scale developer infrastructure, build systems, CI/CD, deployment systems, or production reliability.

 - Can debug across local machines, devboxes, remote caches, monorepos, service dependencies, auth systems, and distributed deploy pipelines.

 - Are comfortable with systems like Bazel, Buildkite, Kubernetes, Temporal, Python/TypeScript services, GitHub workflows, and large monorepo tooling, or can ramp quickly on equivalents.

 - Think in product loops as much as systems loops: you care whether developers can understand and trust the workflow, not just whether a subsystem is technically healthy.

 - Know how to replace repeated manual intervention with policy-backed automation while preserving production safety.

 - Communicate well across teams and can turn ambiguous "this is slow/broken/flaky" reports into crisp owners, hypotheses, metrics, and shipped fixes.

 - Prefer practical measurement over vibes, while still knowing that developer frustration is often the first signal of a real systems problem.

 - Are energized by high-leverage work where a small improvement can save hundreds of engineering hours.

Nice to have:

 - Experience improving developer experience in a very large monorepo.

 - Experience with remote execution, remote caching, hermetic builds, or cache reproducibility.

 - Experience designing CI quarantine, test ownership, merge queue, or auto-revert systems.

 - Experience with progressive delivery, canary/preview/stable deploy pipelines, synthetics, alert quality, and deploy-manager style workflows.

 - Experience building agent-assisted developer workflows, such as automated PR babysitting, CI triage, or conflict resolution.

 - Familiarity with security and access-control constraints around secrets, internal auth, VPN/exit-node networking, and local development.

title: Program Manager, Government Trusted Access
description:
About the Team

OpenAI for Government works with U.S. and allied government institutions to support the responsible adoption of AI across defense, intelligence, federal civilian, state and local, and international public-sector missions. We help public servants use frontier AI in ways that are effective, trusted, and grounded in real-world requirements for safety, reliability, security, compliance, and accountability.



Government Trusted Access programs help eligible public-sector organizations and practitioners use advanced capabilities for approved, high-value work in sensitive domains. These programs bring together OpenAI for Government, Product Policy, Legal, Security, International, Research, User Operations, Technical Success, Global Affairs, and domain experts. Each program has distinct eligibility criteria, safeguards, and decision owners; our job is to make the overall government experience coherent and executable.



About the Role

We are seeking a Program Manager to coordinate OpenAI’s Government Trusted Access portfolio across high-trust domains, such as cyber and bio. You will build and run the operating mechanisms that move government participants from initial interest through review, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, and program improvement.



The right person is a highly organized, low-ego operator who can move between strategy and detail. You are comfortable working across technical, policy, legal, safety, security, customer, and operational teams; you build durable systems without adding unnecessary process; and you communicate clearly when facts, ownership, or requirements are still evolving.



This role is based in Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will:

 - Coordinate government participation across domain-specific Trusted Access programs, including cyber and biology, while helping stand up future programs as the portfolio evolves.

 - Own the end-to-end program operating rhythm across intake, qualification, review, approval, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, renewal, and offboarding.

 - Maintain a clear portfolio view of applicants and participating organizations, access levels, requirements, owners, dependencies, commitments, risks, and decisions needed.

 - Build practical program mechanisms such as roadmaps, ownership maps, decision logs, risk registers, service standards, operating reviews, dashboards, and executive updates.

 - Coordinate cross-functional reviews across OpenAI for Government, Safety, Product Policy, Legal, Security, Product, Research, User Operations, Technical Success, Global Affairs, and domain experts.

 - Preserve clear decision boundaries: ensure the right domain owner makes eligibility, policy, safety, security, and access decisions while keeping the broader process moving.

 - Identify stalled reviews, broken handoffs, unclear ownership, capacity constraints, and recurring operational gaps; bring the right context, options, and recommendation to resolve them.

 - Partner with government-facing teams to set accurate expectations, coordinate participant communications, and ensure commitments are tracked through completion.

 - Define and monitor program health through measures such as review time, backlog age, onboarding completion, activation, support demand, participant outcomes, and operational risk.

 - Turn manual and one-off work into scalable workflows, documentation, training, automation, and tooling while retaining appropriate human judgment for sensitive decisions.

 - Capture lessons across domains and translate them into reusable operating patterns without flattening meaningful differences between programs.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Hold an active TS clearance

 - Have 5–10 years of experience in program management, strategy and operations, product operations, trust and safety, risk operations, support operations, government technology, implementation, or a related field.

 - Have led complex, cross-functional programs from an ambiguous problem statement through launch and steady-state operation.

 - Can build trust and drive alignment without direct authority while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear.

 - Can translate technical, policy, legal, safety, security, and customer requirements into practical workflows and decision structures.

 - Are analytically fluent and comfortable using operational data, dashboards, case-management systems, and lightweight automation to identify bottlenecks and improve program health.

 - Communicate clearly and directly with technical teams, operators, government stakeholders, and executives, especially when evidence is incomplete or tradeoffs are sensitive.

description:

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for dedicated, experienced, and deeply curious individuals to help solve some of the most complex challenges faced by our customers while building the future of post-AGI support alongside us. In this role, you’ll work directly with customers through support tickets and live calls, troubleshooting high-impact issues and resolving novel, often ambiguous technical problems in one of the fastest-moving environments in technology. As AI adoption rapidly accelerates, the work you do will directly support mission-critical systems being built on OpenAI’s platform, serving as a critical line of defense for customers operating at massive scale.

 - Driving operational excellence by identifying opportunities for automation and AI-powered workflows, implementing scalable improvements that increase team efficiency, reducing manual effort, and elevating the overall support experience.

 - Providing occasional holiday and weekend support on call coverage, as needed, to support business and customer needs.

 

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Have 8+ years of experience in User Operations, Engineering, Support Engineering or similar technical roles, ideally within high-growth tech startups or other fast-paced environments.

 - Are comfortable using emerging technologies (ie. Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI API, etc.) to script or engineer code (e.g., Python) for automating repetitive tasks and integrating tools.

Our Federal Civilian and State & Local Government business supports public institutions across a broad range of missions. We help these customers apply frontier AI to public services, knowledge work, research, and mission operations through hands-on delivery, tailored enablement, and collaboration with their teams.

The Strategic Delivery Lead (SDL), Federal Civilian & State and Local Government, will shape and deliver high-impact AI engagements across federal civilian agencies and state and local governments. You will turn customer priorities into practical deployments and sustained use, helping government leaders and mission teams apply OpenAI technology to public services, knowledge discovery, and operational workflows.

This individual contributor role reports to the leader of Federal Civilian and State & Local Government. You will work alongside Account Directors and Applied AI Architects across assigned engagements, coordinating Research, Product, Engineering, Policy, Security, and Enablement resources. Account Directors own commercial strategy, contracts, and quota; you own delivery coordination, adoption, and customer outcomes, without an individual sales quota.

This role is based in Washington, DC, with domestic travel for high-value customer engagements, workshops, and delivery milestones.

 - Build trusted relationships with senior government leaders, program owners, and technical and mission teams to identify priorities and turn senior alignment into actionable engagements.

title: AI Support Engineer - Singapore (Weekend Shift)
description:

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

We’re looking for dedicated, experienced, and deeply curious individuals to help solve some of the most complex challenges faced by our customers while building the future of post-AGI support alongside us. As AI adoption rapidly accelerates, the work you do will directly support mission-critical systems being built on OpenAI’s platform, serving as a critical line of defense for customers operating at massive scale.

Beyond resolving technical issues, you’ll help define what world-class support looks like in an AGI-driven future. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Operations to improve systems, reduce bugs, and elevate the customer experience, while leveraging automation, agents, and our own AI technology to transform how support operates at scale.

This role is based in Singapore. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. To succeed in this position you must be fully fluent in English (spoken and written). Please note that your resume must be submitted in English, and the interview process will be conducted in English.

Note: each person in this role will be expected to work a standard 5x8 work week, with 1 of the days covering weekend shifts each week (e.g., work weeks covering Tuesday - Saturday or Sunday - Thursday)

 - Driving operational excellence by identifying opportunities for automation and AI-powered workflows, implementing scalable improvements that increase team efficiency, reducing manual effort, and elevating the overall support experience.

 - Providing occasional holiday and weekend support on call coverage, as needed, to support business and customer needs.

 - Polished enterprise communication and are calm with high-stakes customers during live incident calls

 - Proven experience building strong relationships with customers and cross-functional partners to drive resolution to complex issues.

title: Growth Lead, France
description:
About the Team

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows.

The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements.

We combine product strategy with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets.

About the Role

We’re looking for a growth lead in France to shape and execute ChatGPT’s growth plans. You’ll partner with the France GM to understand local users, identify the biggest growth opportunities, and turn those priorities into product improvements, funnel optimizations, and performance marketing tests. You’ll work across acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization, collaborating with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Partnerships, and Marketing teams to influence priorities and ship measurable impact. The role combines product growth and funnel optimization with performance marketing: connecting audience, message, creative, and channel learnings to better in-product journeys.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with the France GM, regional teams, and central teams to set a country growth plan and roadmap priorities, with clear hypotheses, owners, dependencies, and measurable outcomes.

 - Use user research, funnel and cohort data, and competitive insight to find local friction and prioritize the opportunities that matter most to users.

 - Run performance marketing tests in collaboration with regional marketers across relevant channels, creators, and partners; use incrementally, CAC, payback, and LTV to decide what to scale.

 - Design and run rigorous experiments across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, and paid conversion; measure incremental impact and iterate. Work with Product, Engineering, Design, and Data Science partners to prototype, test, and ship locally relevant experiences.

 - Partner with regional Marketing and central media teams to brief and prioritize audience, positioning, creative, and channel tests based on the country plan.

 - Own the country growth scorecard across acquisition, retention, paid conversion, and unit economics, distinguishing incremental user and revenue gains and learnings 

 - Connect priority use cases, product improvements, and acquisition plans into a coherent journey from first exposure to repeated value.

 - Run the growth operating cadence with the GM and regional teams, aligning central and local partners on results, trade-offs, dependencies, and next steps.

 - Build and operate product experimentation capabilities, segmentation, lifecycle/user journeys, performance marketing, and growth platform/tooling that can be scaled across markets.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 10+ years of experience across product growth, data science, or growth strategy and operations, with hands-on execution in a fast-moving technology company.

 - A user-first track record of turning local research and behavior into product and growth priorities, then shipping improvements with measurable impact.

 - Strong command of acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization funnels, including technically rigorous experimentation and interpretation.

 - Practical performance marketing experience across audience, channel, creative, and measurement decisions, and the ability to partner effectively with media specialists.

 - Analytical fluency in cohort analysis and growth economics, including incrementality, LTV, CAC, payback, and contribution margin.

 - Experience adapting and running campaigns across markets, using local audience behavior, channels, language, and cultural context to improve relevance and performance at scale.

title: Data Engineer, Hardware & Consumer Devices
description:
About the team

OpenAI is building a new generation of AI-powered consumer devices, creating opportunities to bring increasingly capable AI into people's everyday lives.

Our Data Engineering team is responsible for establishing the foundational data infrastructure that supports the development, manufacturing, launch, and ongoing operation of these products. We're building the systems that connect information across the entire device lifecycle, enabling engineering, operations, and Data Science partners to understand product performance, identify problems, and make better decisions.

This is an early-stage organization with significant greenfield opportunities. We're looking for engineers who want to shape the technical foundations of a rapidly growing business and establish systems that will scale alongside our products.

About the role:

As a Data Engineer, you'll design, build, and scale the data infrastructure that powers OpenAI's hardware and consumer devices organization.

You'll tackle technically challenging problems involving complex data sources, evolving operational requirements, and systems that need to scale from early development through manufacturing and consumer deployment.

Unlike roles focused primarily on supporting individual analytics projects, this position emphasizes building durable, reusable data foundations that enable multiple teams and use cases.

You'll have significant ownership over technical decisions, work closely with partners across engineering, manufacturing, operations, and Data Science, and help define how we approach Data Engineering as the organization grows.

In this role, you will:

 - Build foundational data infrastructure: Design and implement reliable, scalable data pipelines, platforms, and datasets that support hardware development, manufacturing, customer operations, and device performance.

 - Connect complex data ecosystems: Integrate information across manufacturing systems, factory operations, device telemetry, quality assurance, and customer-facing operational systems.

 - Establish durable data models: Develop reusable datasets and data architectures that enable consistent measurement, investigation, and decision-making across multiple teams.

 - Enable manufacturing and quality intelligence: Connect manufacturing conditions and production history with downstream product performance, reliability, returns, and failure signals.

 - Prepare for scale: Design systems that evolve from early-stage development and initial production to increasingly complex operations and large-scale consumer deployment.

 - Partner across disciplines: Work with hardware and software engineers, manufacturing teams, operations leaders, and Data Scientists to translate emerging requirements into robust technical solutions.

 - Shape our technical direction: Help establish engineering standards, architectural principles, data quality practices, and infrastructure decisions that will influence the organization for years to come.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are comfortable making architectural decisions as requirements evolve and the right solutions aren't immediately obvious.

 - Are highly self-directed and can take broad, ambiguous problems from exploration through implementation.

 - Enjoy working directly with cross-functional partners and understanding how technical decisions affect real products and operational outcomes.

 - Have a builder's mentality and are energized by creating foundational systems rather than exclusively optimizing mature infrastructure.

 - Hold a high bar for engineering quality while remaining pragmatic about the speed and flexibility required in an early-stage environment.

Minimum Qualifications:

 - Have exceptional Data Engineering fundamentals and a track record of designing, building, and operating complex data systems.

 - Bring strong technical judgment around data architecture, distributed systems, data modeling, reliability, and scalability.

 - Have experience developing production-grade pipelines and infrastructure across heterogeneous data sources.

Bonus points if you have:

 - Experience with hardware, consumer electronics, connected devices, or IoT.

 - Experience building data infrastructure for manufacturing, factory operations, or supply-chain systems.

 - Familiarity with device telemetry, reliability engineering, product quality, or failure analysis.

 - Experience supporting customer operations, technical support, or Trust & Safety.

 - A track record of building data platforms or foundational infrastructure in a startup or rapidly scaling organization.



Prior hardware experience is not required. We value exceptional engineering ability, intellectual curiosity, and the capacity to learn new domains quickly.

title: Senior Counsel, France
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team supports OpenAI’s mission by addressing complex legal issues arising from the development and deployment of AI. The team brings together expertise in commercial, corporate, employment, privacy, intellectual property, regulatory, tax and litigation matters, and works closely with teams across the company.

About the Role

We’re seeking an experienced, hands-on lawyer to serve as our country lawyer for France, providing broad legal support for our local office with a primary focus on regulatory and policy legal matters affecting OpenAI’s products, operations and business.

You will advise on French and EU regulatory developments, develop practical legal positions and recommendations, and support OpenAI’s engagement with French regulators and policymakers. Working closely with EMEA and global legal colleagues, as well as policy and regulatory affairs teams, you will take ownership of assigned French matters, translate complex legal questions into actionable advice and help ensure that our approach in France is consistent with OpenAI’s wider legal positions.

Alongside your primary focus, you will also provide broader French country legal support, coordinating with specialist teams on local business and operational matters.

We’re looking for someone who can take responsibility for matters, give practical advice, manage competing priorities and bring cross-functional work to a decision. You will work closely with EMEA and global legal colleagues, GA and Policy leaders, applying established specialist guidance, approval processes and escalation routes.

In this role, you will:

 - Advise on regulatory developments and their business implications. Assess existing and emerging French and EU laws, enforcement developments and policy proposals affecting OpenAI. Develop legal positions and practical recommendations, working with GA, Policy, Regulatory, Product, Privacy and other legal teams to translate requirements into action. Serve as a trusted legal partner to local leadership and business teams on the establishment, expansion and day-to-day operation of our French presence. Identify legal dependencies early and translate them into practical options and implementation plans.

 - Support regulatory and policy engagement. Partner with GA, Policy and legal colleagues to prepare for and participate in engagements with French and EU regulators, policymakers and local government. Develop legal analysis, briefing materials, consultation responses and legal input into policy positions, coordinating with the relevant EMEA and global teams.

 - Support French business initiatives. Advise on local partnerships, research and university collaborations, marketing, events and other commercial initiatives, working with Commercial, Product, IP, Privacy and Regulatory Legal as appropriate.

 - Provide coordinated French country legal support. Serve as a local legal partner on French business and operational matters, including local governance, office development, employment and workplace compliance. Identify legal requirements, involve the appropriate specialist teams and help take agreed actions through to implementation, maintaining clear ownership and alignment with OpenAI’s global operating framework.

You might thrive in this role if you:

title: Product Designer, Consumer Verticals
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Consumer Verticals team explores how ChatGPT can become meaningfully more useful in important areas of people’s lives, including health, finance, and emerging agentic experiences.

We work across research, engineering, product, design, and domain experts to turn increasingly capable models into intuitive, trustworthy consumer products. Our work combines the reach of ChatGPT with the depth required to serve distinct user needs responsibly.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead the end-to-end design of new consumer experiences across emerging verticals. You’ll explore how ChatGPT should adapt to different contexts, translate complex model capabilities into clear product interactions, and establish patterns that can scale across multiple domains.

This is a highly generative, zero-to-one role. You’ll move between broad product vision and detailed interaction design, creating prototypes that help teams learn quickly and polished experiences that are ready to ship. You’ll also navigate domains where trust, accuracy, safety, and user agency are essential.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape the product and design direction for purpose-built consumer experiences across areas such as health, finance, and general consumer agents.

 - Design and ship high-quality products from early concepts and prototypes through detailed interaction design and final visual execution.

 - Define how ChatGPT should behave in different domains while preserving a coherent, distinctly OpenAI experience.

 - Explore new interaction models for AI systems that can understand context, support complex decisions, and take action on a user’s behalf.

 - Partner closely with research, engineering, product management, safety, and domain experts to turn technical capabilities into useful and responsible products.

 - Conduct and apply user research to understand the distinct needs, expectations, and risks within each vertical.

 - Balance specialized domain requirements with reusable patterns that can strengthen ChatGPT and accelerate future product development.

 - Contribute to OpenAI’s broader design culture and raise the bar for consumer product craft.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have substantial experience designing and shipping high-quality consumer software at scale.

 - Bring exceptional UX, UI, and interaction design skills, with a high bar for craft in every stage of the work.

 - Are a highly generative product thinker who can explore broadly, develop a strong point of view, and turn ambiguity into clear product direction.

 - Have led zero-to-one initiatives or introduced new product categories, behaviors, or interaction models.

 - Can simplify complex systems without hiding the details users need to make informed decisions.

 - Have strong instincts for trust, safety, transparency, and user control—particularly in consequential or sensitive experiences.

 - Can move fluently between domain-specific problems and broader systems or platform thinking.

title: Physical Network & Structured Cabling Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI is on a bold mission to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure. We are seeking a Data Center Network and Structured Cabling Engineer with 10+ years of experience in designing and implementing optimized network and structured cabling solutions at large data centers buildings and data center campuses.

The Data Center Engineering team is central to this mission defining infrastructure strategy, driving technical innovation, working with research to set performance benchmarks, and developing reference designs that enable rapid, scalable global deployment.

As part of this team, you will help design and deliver next-generation data center infrastructure optimized for AI workloads. You’ll collaborate across research, site selection, design, construction, commissioning, hardware engineering, deployment, operations, and global partners to bring OpenAI’s infrastructure vision to life.

Role Summary

As a Physical Network & Structured Cabling Engineer, you will own the design, implementation, and quality assurance of structured cabling and physical network infrastructure across OpenAI’s global data center footprint. This role bridges design, construction, and operations, ensuring that every layer of our physical networking from fiber trunks to copper patching meets the highest standards of performance, reliability, and scalability.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design and specify physical network infrastructure across data center buildings and campuses, including fiber and copper cabling, network rooms, rack layouts, cable trays, and duct bank pathways. Coordinate with other engineering disciplines to ensure network infrastructure space, power, cooling, and operational requirements are incorporated into the overall design

 - Develop standards, reference designs, and installation guidelines for structured cabling and physical network deployments.

 - Translate logical network architectures and hardware connectivity requirements into scalable physical designs, including fiber topology, port connectivity, patching, redundancy, and capacity planning, in partnership with network engineering and operations teams.

 - Provide technical direction to design consultants, cabling vendors, and installation contractors, resolving scope gaps and ensuring designs are constructible and meet network requirements.

 - Define installation quality and acceptance criteria, and oversee inspection, testing, commissioning, and turnover of structured cabling systems.

 - Lead physical network design reviews, coordinate clash detection and resolution with other disciplines, and conduct site inspections to verify installation quality and conformance with design and operational requirements.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve issues during build, commissioning, and handover phases to ensure network readiness.

 - Develop and maintain physical network documentation, including design requirements, drawings, port maps, cable schedules, bills of materials, labeling standards, and as-built records.

 - Provide feedback to design and operations teams to drive continuous improvement of physical network standards.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, or related field, or equivalent experience.

 - 10+ years of experience designing and delivering physical network infrastructure and structured cabling systems for large-scale data centers, including responsibility for design decisions, construction coordination, and operational readiness.

 - Strong understanding of data center network topologies and high-speed optical connectivity, including transceivers, fiber types, breakout configurations, connector and polarity schemes, and optical loss budgets.

 - Expertise in industry standards such as ANSI/TIA, BICSI and other relevant structured cabling guidelines.

 - Proven ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams and external vendors on large-scale projects.

 - Strong skills in reviewing and interpreting technical drawings, cable schedules, and documentation management.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Willingness to travel frequently to global data center sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Master’s degree in Engineering, or relevant certifications such as BICSI, RCDD, or equivalent.

 - Experience with hyperscale cloud, AI, or high-performance computing environments.

 - Proficiency in 2D and 3D engineering tools (e.g., CAD, Revit) for infrastructure design and clash detection analysis.

 - Experience with structured connectivity data and automation for generating and validating port maps, cable schedules, bills of materials, and labels.

 - Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills for physical layer systems and issues.

Professional Services provides specialist expertise and capacity across OpenAI, spanning consulting and advisory, finance and accounting, legal, people-related services and managed services. title: Vendor Security Technical Program Manager
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Vendor Security team helps internal teams work securely with external products, services, and partners. Our work spans software, infrastructure, hardware, professional and managed services, vendor-provided workforces, data, and research. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company.

About the Role

We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work.

You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next.

In this role, you will:

 - Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scoping, assessment, decision, treatment, and reassessment when material facts change. Make assessment decisions independently and use judgment about when to involve peers, specialists, or leadership. Route formal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners.

 - Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI.

 - Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear.

 - Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works.

 - Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers.

 - Work with Legal, Procurement, and vendors on security addenda. Evaluate proposed terms and deviations against the engagement, explain their security implications, and develop workable positions with the appropriate decision owners. Legal leads wording and negotiation.

 - Learn from internal customers, agree priorities with the Vendor Security lead, and define the requirements, roadmap, and success measures for the bounded programs, products, and services you own.

 - Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement.

 - Lead delivery across Security and partner teams. Translate goals into technical requirements, milestones, and delivery plans; influence implementation choices; identify systemic risks; resolve dependencies and disagreements; and carry commitments through completion.

 - Use casework, incidents, threat information, and customer feedback to improve decisions and the program. As priorities change, recommend what to do next and explain the tradeoffs and effects on existing commitments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have independently assessed consequential third-party, supply-chain, or comparable security risks, and can apply that judgment to unfamiliar vendor technologies and operating models.

 - Understand security principles and controls, including data protection, access management, application security, prevention, detection, and response. Can reason about architecture, identity, APIs, data flows, logging, integrations, and whether controls work.

 - Know relevant frameworks and standards, including ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and SOC 2, and can use them to inform an assessment of the actual engagement.

 - Have translated security findings and requirements into practical contractual positions with Legal, Procurement, and vendor representatives.

 - Have delivered useful products or workflow improvements, tested expected behavior and failure cases, learned from users, and owned performance after launch.

 - Can use Codex or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build, run, inspect, and test working solutions.

 - Have independently delivered cross-functional programs, turned ambiguity into technical requirements and plans, and adapted priorities to achieve measurable outcomes. Can judge when to build, use existing systems, or engage partners to resolve blockers.

 - Build constructive relationships with Security, Engineering, Product, Privacy, Legal, business teams, and vendors. Communicate complex security issues clearly in writing and conversation, including your recommendation, supporting evidence, and relevant tradeoffs.

 - Question assumptions, try thoughtful new approaches, investigate unfamiliar systems, and revise your judgment when new evidence changes the situation.

description:

We work with customers across industries to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

As the Manager of Applied AI Architects, you will lead a team of senior technical leaders responsible for the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value for OpenAI's largest and most complex customers. description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable and Supplier Master Data Operations provide the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience.

About the Role

OpenAI’s compute infrastructure depends on controlled execution of significant supplier spend. As Senior Manager, Accounts Payable — Compute, you will own payment readiness and material exceptions across large-value, business-critical obligations. Complex agreements evolve through amendments to pricing, capacity, service credits, billing mechanics, legal entities, and payment schedules. You will translate approved obligations into accurate, timely payments while navigating supplier disputes, late approvals, close deadlines, and cross-system dependencies.

We’re looking for a hands-on technical and operational leader who can interpret complex payment terms, reconcile financial data, diagnose system failures, and build scalable workflows. Coordinating across multiple Compute Finance and Accounting teams is a core responsibility: you will establish decision owners, align deadlines, and move interdependent work forward in parallel. You will set the compute AP operating plan and lead delivery with Procurement, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing processing teams, with measurable improvements in controls, service, and capacity.

Location: This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the compute invoice-to-payment operating plan, prioritize material exceptions, and lead supplier escalations across complex, high-value obligations and tight payment deadlines.

 - Interpret executed contracts and approved amendments affecting pricing, capacity, credits, billing mechanics, entities, and payment schedules; translate them into invoice-validation, PO/change-order, approval, control, and payment requirements.

 - Personally investigate discrepancies, supplier disputes, missing credits, duplicate risks, and PO coverage gaps. Trace records, field mappings, approval statuses, and sync failures across procurement and ERP systems; resolve root causes with accountable Finance, Procurement, supplier, and Systems partners.

 - Lead a payment-readiness cadence across Compute Finance and Accounting teams, consolidate the complete obligation and payment view, and resolve dependencies across charge validation, PO coverage, approvals, funding, and close. Track decision owners, deadlines, blockers, and escalation paths so material payments move forward as approval lands.

 - Confirm supplier, site, entity, tax, payment-method, and approval readiness with the relevant owners before payment release.

 - Coordinate funding forecasts and close-period payments with Treasury; reconcile invoice aging, payment registers, and bank/settlement evidence to support Accounting’s completeness and cutoff conclusions.

 - Design matching tolerances, validation rules, exception routing, evidence requirements, and escalation thresholds with control and accounting partners, preserving independent verification and segregation of duties.

 - Map compute workload and usable capacity by task and complexity, assign eligible work across employees, contractors, and shared-service teams, and maintain trained backups and close coverage. Coach task owners and backups, strengthen execution standards, and build greater team autonomy.

 - Set a prioritized improvement roadmap tied to compute business needs. Own requirements and acceptance criteria for workflow and AI improvements; lead operational testing and adoption with Finance Systems and Enablement, verify reconciliation and fallback, and measure service, risk, and verified capacity outcomes.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex, high-value supplier obligations and material exceptions from executed contract through invoice approval, payment, and settlement.

 - Bring strong judgment on controls, segregation of duties, supplier verification, reconciliations, and close support in an audited environment.

 - Can interpret complex pricing, capacity, credit, billing, and payment terms and translate contract amendments into executable workflows, matching rules, and clear decision ownership.

 - Have led coordination across multiple finance and accounting teams on material payments, reconciled competing priorities and deadlines, and established clear decisions, handoffs, and escalation paths with suppliers and partners.

 - Have independently led cross-functional operating improvements and delivery teams, built demand-and-capacity plans, maintained peak and backup coverage, and demonstrated measurable results while staying close to execution.

 - Can independently reconcile large financial datasets using advanced spreadsheets or comparable analytical tools, establish complete populations and control totals, and diagnose ERP workflow, data, and integration failures. Oracle Fusion and Zip experience is helpful.

 - Have demonstrated practical application of AI in finance or operations, with measurable gains in accuracy, speed, or capacity. Can translate business and control requirements into testable workflows and lead UAT, with human review, exception handling, reconciliation, fallback, and ongoing monitoring.

About the Team

The SMB Ads team helps businesses discover, adopt, and grow with OpenAI’s advertising solutions. As we scale globally, we are building a high-performing sales organization that combines operational excellence, strong customer experiences, and AI-native ways of working.

We partner closely with Sales, Revenue Operations, Finance, Product, Enablement, Program Management, and external BPO partners to drive advertiser acquisition, activation, revenue growth, and retention.



About the Role

We are hiring a BPO Lead to build and scale the outsourced operating model that supports our Ads business in North America and globally.



This is a builder role. You will design the governance, performance systems, capacity plans, quality programs, and accountability mechanisms that enable our BPO partners to deliver exceptional commercial outcomes. You will work across internal teams and external partner leadership to improve seller productivity, advertiser growth, forecasting accuracy, and operational quality.



This is a highly cross-functional individual contributor role that sits at the intersection of Ads Sales, SMB, Revenue Operations, Finance, Enablement, Product, Program Management, and external BPO leadership. You will help define how OpenAI operates with external partners and build the systems, processes, and accountability mechanisms that enable the business to scale.



In this role, you will:

Build and scale BPO operating models, governance structures, and performance frameworks for Ads

 - Drive results across revenue, pipeline, advertiser acquisition, activation, retention, seller productivity, and quality

 - Lead business reviews and executive governance forums with BPO partners and internal stakeholders

 - Develop scorecards, forecasts, inspection mechanisms, and escalation processes that surface risks early

 - Improve sales quality through playbooks, QA frameworks, coaching programs, and performance analysis

 - Partner with Sales, Revenue Operations, Product, Enablement, Finance, and Program teams on new products, markets, and sales motions

 - Create workforce and capacity plans aligned to business demand and growth forecasts

 - Determine which customer segments and sales motions should be handled by BPO partners versus internal teams

 - Use AI, automation, and scalable systems to improve execution, visibility, and seller productivity



You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 5+ years of experience in vendor operations, commercial operations, outsourced sales, or a scaled revenue organization

 - Experience in Ads, advertiser growth, performance marketing, or a comparable SMB sales motion

 - Working knowledge of sales funnels, forecasting, advertiser activation, spend growth, retention, and churn

 - Experience improving operating processes, scorecards, quality programs, or capacity plans across vendors or markets

 - Strong analytical, operational, and communication skills, with the ability to turn data into clear actions and work effectively across teams

 - Interest in using AI and automation to improve execution, visibility, and seller productivity

title: International Payroll Operations
description:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission.

OpenAI’s Payroll team is responsible for timely and accurate processing of payroll and ensuring compliance with all statutory regulations.

About the Role

At OpenAI, payroll is not a back-office function — it is mission-critical infrastructure. We are seeking a seasoned International Payroll lead to scale and continuously improve the global payroll and payroll-support ecosystem that serves one of the fastest-growing and most technically sophisticated organizations in the world.

This role is based in our Dublin, Ireland office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead the international payroll processing team and oversee end-to-end payroll delivery across EMEA and APAC, ensuring employees are paid accurately, on time, and in compliance with local requirements.

 - Own day-to-day operations with outsourced payroll and BPO partners, including payroll calendars, inputs, reconciliations, service-level performance, quality standards, issue resolution, and escalations.

 - Lead the payroll workstream for global expansion and new-country launches, including payroll registrations, in-country vendor setup, implementation, testing, systems integration, and go-live readiness.

 - Partner with People, Finance, Tax, Legal, Benefits, Equity, and Treasury teams to ensure accurate upstream inputs, funding, accounting, and downstream reporting.

 - Draft and maintain payroll documentation, process maps, operating procedures, and internal controls to support compliance, audit readiness, and business continuity.

 - Proactively identify and resolve payroll discrepancies and employee inquiries within SLAs, determine root causes, and implement controls that prevent recurrence.

 - Use data, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve controls, reduce manual work, and increase the scalability and effectiveness of international payroll operations.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 6+ years of progressive experience in international payroll operations, preferably in a fast-paced or high-growth environment.

 - Demonstrated experience leading multi-country payroll delivery across EMEA and APAC, including management of outsourced payroll or BPO providers.

 - Hands-on experience supporting new-country payroll implementations, vendor onboarding, testing, and systems integrations.

 - Hands-on experience using AI tools to enhance, automate, and strengthen payroll workflows and controls.

 - Strong working knowledge of international payroll regulations, tax withholding, social insurance, statutory reporting, and standard payroll practices.

 - Hands-on experience with Workday HCM and global payroll systems.

 - Ability to independently manage priorities, take ownership of outcomes, and deliver high-quality work under tight deadlines.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.

 - Clear and concise communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, HR, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

title: Pricing Operations Lead
description:
About the Team

The Pricing & Monetization team is responsible for how our products create and capture value. We partner closely with Product, GTM, Finance, and Systems teams to design pricing models, packaging, and commercial strategies that support adoption, growth, and long-term scaling of the business.

To thrive in this team, you need to be a proactive problem-solver who excels at bringing structure to ambiguous challenges. Our work demands strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and precision in execution. Team members succeed when they are analytical, detail-oriented, skilled at balancing multiple priorities, and passionate about driving high-stakes projects forward to deliver meaningful results.

About the Role

We are looking for a Pricing Operations Lead to help translate pricing and packaging decisions into clear, scalable execution. You will work closely with pricing leaders and cross-functional partners across Product, Engineering, Billing, Finance, and GTM to ensure pricing changes are implemented accurately, system requirements are well managed, and launch decisions move from strategy to reality with discipline.

You should be comfortable operating at the intersection of business judgment, systems thinking, and program management. This role will help shape the operating backbone for pricing implementation, support teams developing billing and related monetization systems, and ensure the pricing team's needs are represented clearly in cross-functional planning and execution.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead the operational execution of pricing and packaging decisions from approval through implementation and launch

 - Translate pricing strategy, policies, and launch decisions into clear business requirements for billing, quoting, revenue, and related systems teams

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, Billing, Finance, and GTM teams to manage dependencies, scope tradeoffs, testing needs, and launch readiness

 - Own pricing-related requirement intake and prioritization on behalf of the pricing team, ensuring requests are clear, well managed, and tied to business needs

 - Support the design and implementation of new product, SKU, packaging, and billing configurations as pricing changes move into production

 - Establish lightweight but effective pricing operations processes, including governance, documentation, sign-offs, and issue tracking

 - Identify recurring friction in pricing execution and drive improvements that reduce ambiguity, delays, and rework

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 6+ years of experience leading pricing operations or closely related monetization, commercialization, or revenue operations work

 - Have a strong track record of helping implement complex pricing or packaging decisions across cross-functional teams

 - Can translate pricing intent into practical system requirements, launch plans, operating workflows, and stakeholder decisions

 - Have experience partnering closely with billing systems, product, engineering, finance, and go-to-market teams

 - Are highly organized and comfortable managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, risks, and timelines at once

 - Communicate clearly with both business and technical audiences, and can drive accountability without creating unnecessary process

 - Care deeply about operational precision, customer clarity, and building systems that scale as pricing complexity grows

 - Are a self-starter who can roll up your sleeves and operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-ambiguity environment

title: ITAV Event Technical Producer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s IT organization supports the mission of deploying artificial general intelligence (AGI) for the benefit of all. Our team is committed to providing seamless technological support and solutions to ensure that all OpenAI employees are well-equipped and connected. This enables them to contribute effectively towards our AI research, corporate operations and product initiatives.

About the Role

As an ITAV Event Technical Producer at OpenAI, you will lead technical production for complex internal and external events across multiple sites, from early planning through rehearsal and live delivery. You will partner with internal stakeholders and technical teams to translate event requirements into clear production plans. You will coordinate internal and external crews, direct large, distributed shows and coordinate cross-site handoffs, and use your technical expertise to resolve production challenges and make informed tradeoffs. You will also build reusable production practices and AI workflows, improve how teams deliver events, and mentor peers and junior crew members.

This is a full-time, onsite role requiring five days per week in San Francisco. Travel to other OpenAI locations is required as needed for assigned events.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead technical production for complex internal, hybrid, and distributed events from early planning and scoping through rehearsal, live delivery, and debrief.

 - Align Internal Comms, Marketing, Brand Experience, and Workplace on audience goals, requirements, scope, dependencies, and decision owners. Turn ambiguous or competing needs into an agreed production plan and readiness criteria.

 - Configure and operate live audio, video switching, cameras, playback, conferencing, streaming, and recording systems for the agreed production.

 - Integrate the run of show across sites and lead multiple crews globally for all-company events. Align technical cues, rehearsals, content handoffs, schedules, and contingencies with partner teams to deliver one cohesive event.

 - Lead rehearsals and validate the complete audience experience, including remote contribution, playback, recording, and tested backup paths.

 - Independently prioritize technical production tradeoffs and lead risk reviews and incident response. Resolve ambiguity within your scope, and seek guidance for complex situations or decisions owned by event, staffing, budget, or engineering partners.

 - Build reusable production plans, show files, runbooks, and change-control practices. Coach peers and junior crew members to use them independently and verify improvements in readiness, troubleshooting, and execution.

 - Set a prioritized roadmap for production improvements using audience feedback, debriefs, and recurring failures. Lead workflow changes across teams and define permanent-system improvements with AV Engineering.

 - Identify repeatable production work and build AI and agentic workflows with partner teams. Validate results, establish operating and maintenance ownership, support adoption, and measure preparation effort or reliability improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Experience leading complex live or hybrid productions across multiple teams, from ambiguous requirements through rehearsal, delivery, and debrief.

 - Advanced expertise in multiple live-production domains, such as audio, video, conferencing, streaming, or AV-over-IP, and the ability to diagnose complex interactions across the complete signal path.

 - Experience configuring and operating professional production systems and creating reusable show files or control workflows.

 - Practical AV-over-IP and networking knowledge sufficient to troubleshoot live media, timing, and connectivity with engineering partners.

 - Experience independently resolving ambiguous production problems, setting detailed plans, and prioritizing tradeoffs while seeking guidance when complexity or decision authority requires it.

 - Demonstrated ownership of rehearsals, technical readiness, failover testing, and calm incident response for high-priority productions.

 - Ability to lead crews and influence partner teams without reporting authority, with clear boundaries for content, brand, budget, staffing, and engineering decisions.

 - Experience working with communications, marketing, brand or creative experience, Workplace, and technical partners on complex events, including sensitive planning and late changes.

 - Experience building reusable production frameworks and validated AI workflows, guiding team adoption, and mentoring peers or junior staff with measurable improvements in their capability.

 - Experience with multi-space or multi-location productions and sensitive executive events is a plus.

 - Experience with systems such as Q-SYS, Dante, Ross, Vizrt, or comparable production platforms is a plus.

title: Deal Operations, EMEA
description:
About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across EMEA by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for EMEA account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for EMEA account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

 - Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

 - Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers.

 - Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines.

 - Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders.

 - Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution.

 - Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information.

 - Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls.

 - Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support.

 - Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment.

 - Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes.

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

 - Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

 - Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

 - Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

 - Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

 - A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

title: People Technology Analyst, Workday PATT & Benefits
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s People team helps us hire, support, and retain the people who will safely build and deploy artificial intelligence that benefits humanity.

The People Technology team brings together our enterprise people systems and the engineers building new internal products and AI-powered tools. We work across the People organization to improve the employee experience, simplify operations, and build technology that supports OpenAI’s global growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a People Technology Analyst with deep expertise in Workday Absence, Time Tracking, and Benefits. You’ll independently own configuration, ongoing support, and improvements across these areas, including benefits for our US and international employees, from day one.

You’ll work closely with Benefits, People Operations, Payroll, Finance, and Engineering to translate complex requirements into reliable systems and straightforward employee experiences. You should be comfortable configuring Workday yourself, tracing issues across modules and integrations, and owning improvements from the first conversation through launch and ongoing support.

As part of our combined People Technology team, you’ll also help identify where automation, AI, and custom tools can improve how we work. You’ll bring the domain expertise needed to make those solutions useful and dependable.

In this role, you will:

 - Own Workday configuration and improvements across Absence, Time Tracking, and Benefits, including the connections between leave, time worked, and benefits eligibility.

 - Design and maintain absence plans, accruals, eligibility rules, leave processes, time entry rules, calculations, validations, and approvals for a growing global workforce.

 - Partner with the Payroll systems owner to ensure absence, time tracking, and benefits data flows accurately into payroll. Investigate source data issues and test downstream impacts of changes in your areas.

 - Independently own US and international benefits configuration, including benefit plans, eligibility rules, enrollment events, life events, coverage levels, and rates.

 - Lead open enrollment systems readiness, including configuration, testing, launch, and support. Partner with technical teams and benefits vendors to maintain and troubleshoot integrations.

 - Lead Absence, Time Tracking, and Benefits systems work for new countries and entities, policy changes, and evolving employee needs. Partner with functional owners to translate local requirements into configuration.

 - Own projects from discovery and prioritization through configuration, testing, release, documentation, and adoption. Stay accountable for how the solution performs after launch.

 - Partner with engineers to improve integrations and build automation or AI-assisted workflows that reduce manual work and make employee support easier.

 - Maintain system security, data quality, reporting, and change controls. Resolve production issues and address their underlying causes.

 - Create clear documentation and training that helps employees, managers, and People teams use our systems effectively.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Deep, hands-on Workday expertise across Absence and Time Tracking, with experience designing, configuring, testing, and supporting connected workflows across both.

 - Demonstrated experience independently owning Workday Benefits configuration for US and international programs, including open enrollment, eligibility, life events, and connections to benefits vendors.

 - An understanding of how time, absence, and benefits data flows into payroll and other downstream systems, with the ability to test changes and troubleshoot issues with the relevant system owners.

 - Experience translating complex policies and business requirements into maintainable system designs, including country-specific configurations.

 - Strong Workday technical skills, including business processes, calculated fields, reporting, security, and data loads, along with the ability to troubleshoot integrations with technical partners.

 - Ownership of systems through implementation and ongoing operations, with a record of improving reliability and the experience of the people using them.

 - Good product judgment. You ask questions, understand the underlying problem, prioritize thoughtfully, and evaluate whether a change made things better.

 - Clear communication and the ability to work across People, Payroll, Benefits, Finance, and Engineering.

 - Comfort working through ambiguity, balancing urgent operational needs with longer-term improvements, and following through on details.

 - Global Absence, Time Tracking, or Benefits implementations and new country or entity launches.

 - Collaboration with software engineers on internal products, integrations, or workflow automation.

 - Practical use of AI to improve systems work, documentation, testing, or employee support.

 - Relevant Workday certifications or Workday Pro credentials.

title: Integrated Marketing Manager, Hardware
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to help translate our products, their value propositions, and our broader brand strategy into audience-specific, globally relevant marketing programs. You’ll shape how people discover, understand, adopt, and engage with our products across markets and stages of the customer journey. You’ll connect product narratives, audience insight, cultural context, and business goals into strategies that make advanced technology feel clear, useful, and human.

This is a high-impact individual contributor role for a marketer who understands how product marketing, brand strategy, audience research, and international growth work together. You’ll develop segmentation frameworks, lifecycle and go-to-market programs, regional insights, and partnership opportunities; then work across product marketing, growth, creative, partnerships, analytics, and regional teams to bring them to life. Your work will connect launches, product education, customer engagement, and ongoing storytelling into a coherent journey from awareness to advocacy.

To us, creativity is a team sport. Ideas get better when you talk them through and build on each other’s thinking. We value curiosity over certainty, kindness over ego, and the ability to balance craft with decisiveness.

In this role, you will:

 - Translate complex product capabilities, use cases, and value propositions into clear, differentiated messaging that is relevant to distinct audiences without losing accuracy, nuance, or the product’s ambition.

 - Develop audience segmentation frameworks based on customer needs, behaviors, use cases, regions, industries, and stages of the customer journey.

 - Create audience-specific messaging and campaign strategies for groups such as creators, builders, professionals, students, consumers, and emerging-market users.

 - Lead cross-functional marketing programs end to end for defined audiences or initiatives, with minimal oversight, setting priorities across awareness, acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and advocacy.

 - Lead research efforts including customer interviews, surveys, social listening, competitive analysis, market trends, and behavioral data.

 - Turn research and performance signals into actionable audience personas, messaging frameworks, briefs, campaign recommendations, and market insights.

 - Identify cultural, regional, and language-specific opportunities across global markets, and help adapt global campaigns for local audiences while maintaining a consistent brand voice.

 - Develop go-to-market plans for new campaigns, product features, audience programs, partnerships, and market expansions.

 - Identify partnership opportunities with creators, developers, communities, platforms, industry groups, and other audience ecosystems.

 - Align partners across product marketing, growth, CRM, creative, analytics, partnerships, and regional marketing; resolve tradeoffs and shape creative direction to deliver coordinated customer journeys.

 - Measure campaign and audience performance, using data to improve messaging, segmentation, customer journeys, regional strategies, and future marketing investments.

 - Build reusable campaign processes and playbooks, and coach peers and junior teammates to improve planning, creative collaboration, and execution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 5–8 years of experience in product marketing, brand marketing, lifecycle marketing, growth marketing, audience strategy, partnerships, or related fields.

 - Bring deep familiarity with AI products, foundation models, generative AI capabilities and limitations, and common user workflows; this is a critical qualification for the role.

 - Have experience translating complex technology and technical product capabilities into clear, compelling, differentiated customer value propositions.

 - Are a strategic thinker who can turn audience insight, cultural context, product strategy, and business goals into a compelling point of view and an actionable marketing system.

 - Can move fluidly between big-picture strategy and hands-on execution: building the framework, writing the brief, launching the program, and reviewing results.


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience working with creators, developers, communities, partnerships, or other distinct customer segments.

 - Experience working across cultures, regions, or international markets.

 - Experience with experimentation, performance measurement, social listening, and translating signals into strategic recommendations.

 - Experience in consumer technology, emerging products, developer tools, enterprise products, or other fast-changing categories.
