title: Dedicated Support Engineer - London
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

In this role, you will:

 - Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

 - Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

 - Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

 - Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

 - Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

 - Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

 - Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

 - Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

 - Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

 - Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

 - Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

 - Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

 - Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

 - Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

 - Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

 - Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

 - Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

 - Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

 - Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

 - Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

 - Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

 - Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

 - Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

 - Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale.

title: Software Engineer, Shop/Feed Ads
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Monetization team is a new cross-functional group spanning engineering, product, research, and design. We are building the foundational systems that will help OpenAI scale access to intelligence responsibly.

Our mission is to create user-first, privacy-preserving monetization products—including next-generation ads experiences—that strengthen trust, expand economic opportunity, and support OpenAI’s long-term innovation. We believe monetization should deliver clear user value, uphold rigorous privacy and safety standards, and sustain a healthy ecosystem for developers and businesses.

The team operates in a greenfield environment, moving quickly through prototyping, experimentation, and iterative deployment. We partner closely across Product, Design, and Research to bring new capabilities into real-world systems at global scale.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to lead the design and development of the systems that turn advertiser feeds (eg. retail feeds, travel feeds etc.) into relevant, reliably delivered ads. In this foundational role, you will build across the full ads lifecycle—from ingesting and organizing retailer or travel catalogs into efficient retrieval systems, supporting ranking models, and serving ads at scale.

This role is well suited to an engineer with direct experience in product ads retrieval, ranking, and delivery, along with a strong understanding of merchant feeds and shopping systems such as Google Shopping, YouTube product ads, or Amazon. We also welcome engineers with Senior Staff-level or greater scope who have deep ownership of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing, ads serving, or closely related distributed systems.

You will independently own complex systems, make sound technical tradeoffs, and help define the architecture and roadmap for Shopping/Travel/Feed Ads. You will collaborate closely with Ads ML, Ads Delivery, Product, Design, and Research to connect accurate, fresh advertiser feed information with useful ads experiences in ChatGPT.

This role is based in San Francisco and Mountain View. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Design and build pipelines that ingest, validate, normalize, and refresh merchant product feeds, keeping catalog information accurate and available for serving.

 - Develop scalable catalog storage and indexing systems that make large inventories searchable and reflect changes in product availability, pricing, and attributes.

 - Build search and retrieval systems that efficiently identify relevant, eligible products across merchant catalogs.

 - Partner with Ads ML to connect product retrieval with ranking models through dependable interfaces, features, and serving infrastructure.

 - Engineer low-latency, high-throughput ads delivery systems with strong reliability and correctness guarantees.

 - Design real-time event pipelines and distributed storage that support catalog freshness, serving decisions, and downstream feedback.

 - Build observability and quality controls to detect feed errors, stale inventory, indexing delays, and serving issues.

 - Define technical direction and drive complex projects from early prototypes through production deployment and operation.

 - Operate systems with high engineering rigor through testing, monitoring, privacy and security reviews, and strong operational practices.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, with direct ownership of product ads retrieval, ranking infrastructure, or delivery.

 - Understand merchant feeds and shopping systems, including how catalog quality, product availability, and freshness affect relevance and ads performance.

 - Have built systems for shopping or product ads at platforms such as Google Shopping, YouTube, Amazon, or a comparable environment.

 - Alternatively, have operated at Senior Staff-level scope or above, leading the architecture and delivery of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing platforms, ads serving, or related backend systems.

 - Have built low-latency, high-throughput services and data pipelines with demanding reliability and correctness requirements.

 - Can reason across ingestion, storage, indexing, retrieval, ranking, and serving, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between freshness, relevance, latency, and cost.

 - Are comfortable partnering with machine-learning teams to bring ranking models and signals into dependable production systems.

 - Can define technical direction in an ambiguous 0→1 environment and independently drive complex work across teams.

 - Communicate clearly and make technical decisions grounded in user value, merchant experience, and long-term system health.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Total Rewards team plays a critical role in attracting, rewarding, and retaining world-class talent in support of our mission to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The team designs and delivers compensation and benefits programs that are competitive, equitable, innovative, and scalable, while balancing global strategy, local market dynamics, employee experience, and long-term sustainability.



About the Role

OpenAI is seeking an APAC Total Rewards Business Partner to lead and support compensation initiatives and provide regional benefits execution and operational support across the region as we continue to expand our global footprint. This role will serve as a key regional partner, helping translate OpenAI’s global Total Rewards strategy into programs and practices that reflect local market needs, regulatory requirements, and the evolving needs of our employees.

In this role, you will partner closely with regional leadership, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, People Operations, Finance, Payroll, Legal, and external partners to design, implement, and manage compensation and benefits programs across APAC. You will operate as both a strategic advisor and hands-on practitioner, balancing global consistency with regional flexibility while maintaining a high bar for employee experience and operational excellence.

This role is based in Singapore and we use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the Singapore office per week.



In this role, you will:

 - Regional Total Rewards Partnership: Serve as a trusted Total Rewards advisor across APAC, providing strategic and practical guidance on compensation, benefits, market practices, and complex employee matters as the region scales.

 - Compensation Strategy & Design: Support the development and evolution of base pay structures, incentive programs, equity frameworks, and other compensation programs to ensure competitiveness, internal consistency, and alignment with OpenAI’s global compensation philosophy.

Provide regional support for benefits rollouts, vendor coordination, employee communications and operational issue resolution, and surface local insights to inform programme decisions.

 - Employee Experience & Communication: Develop clear, thoughtful communications that help employees and leaders understand and navigate Total Rewards programs, including compensation processes, benefits enrollment, and program changes.

 - Operational Excellence & Automation: Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and scale Total Rewards processes and tools while strengthening data integrity, controls, and the overall operating model.



You might thrive in this role if you have:

title: Product Manager, Financial Services
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI is building AI products for serious professional work. We’re going deep on finance with a committed team focused on unlocking the potential of AI in this vertical: working closely with industry experts and users to build bespoke solutions that help finance professionals do real work.

OpenAI’s Financial Services team works closely with customers to understand where AI can improve the economics and quality of financial work: faster diligence, broader research coverage, sharper client materials, more accurate models, and better investment analysis. Our work spans workflows across investment banking, equity research, private equity, asset management, wealth management, insurance, and other parts of finance. We bring together OpenAI’s models, financial data, and enterprise knowledge to build products that fit how financial professionals work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Product Manager to help define and build OpenAI’s financial services products. Reporting to the GM of Financial Services, you will own product strategy, roadmap, and execution for key experiences, taking them from customer discovery and early prototypes through launch, adoption, and iteration. This is a hands-on role. You will spend time with bankers, investors, analysts, and other finance professionals; build and test early product experiences; and work closely with Engineering, Design, Research, and customer-facing teams to ship. You should have strong judgment about both the product experience and the work it produces. You will also form a vision for how AI can change the financial services space and can translate that into product execution.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own product strategy and priorities. Work with the GM to identify the most valuable customer problems and translate them into a clear roadmap. Make decisions about what to build, what to defer, and where partners or shared OpenAI capabilities can best meet the need.

 - Go deep on financial workflows. Sit with customers, observe how they work, and understand the documents they create, data they trust, tools they use, and standards they apply. Use those insights to design experiences that customers return to in their daily work.

 - Build and ship. Create working prototypes, demos, example outputs, and product requirements using Codex and other OpenAI tools. Partner with Engineering and Design to turn early concepts into reliable products, resolve dependencies, and drive delivery through launch and iteration.

 - Raise the bar for quality and trust. Work with Research and Engineering to turn real finance tasks and product failures into evaluations, datasets, and model feedback. Define what good looks like across accuracy, source traceability, completeness, and ease of review, while making practical tradeoffs across quality, latency, reliability, and cost.

 - Make products work inside financial institutions. Translate integration, data-access, privacy, security, and review requirements into product decisions. Work across Legal, Security, Partnerships, and core product teams to address deployment barriers and determine which needs require finance-specific solutions.

 - Measure results and drive adoption. Define success through task completion, output acceptance, repeat usage, time saved, and business impact. Combine product data, evaluations, and customer feedback to guide investment. Partner with GTM and customer-facing teams on pilots, onboarding, and launches, then use what you learn to improve the product.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have a track record of taking complex products from discovery through launch and sustained adoption, as a product manager, founder, or builder with substantial product ownership.

 - Understand financial work well enough to earn credibility with demanding practitioners. You may have built products for financial institutions or worked directly in investment banking, investing, equity research, corporate development, or related fields.

 - Combine strong product taste with attention to detail. You care about making complex workflows feel simple and can judge both the experience and the quality of its outputs.

 - Work comfortably with engineers and researchers on model behavior, data quality, integrations, and evaluations. You can distinguish a model limitation from a data, workflow, or product-design problem.

 - Use AI deeply in your own work and build prototypes to test ideas. You are willing to teach, onboard, debug, and inspect outputs alongside customers.

 - Know how to choose useful goals and metrics, test assumptions, and change priorities when the evidence changes.

 - Bring sound judgment about privacy, trust, and accuracy in consequential professional work.

 - Take ownership in ambiguous situations, drive decisions across teams you do not manage, and communicate clearly. You can set direction and stay close to the details required to ship.

title: Ads Marketing Manager, Japan
description:
About the team

OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for businesses to connect with customers in new ways.

The Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth.




About the role

As Japan Ads Marketing Manager, you will help build OpenAI’s advertising business in Japan, with a primary focus on growing small and medium-sized advertisers.  This is a hands-on, zero-to-one opportunity to establish the programs, agency engagement, and local marketing approaches that will shape our growth in Japan.

You will own the market’s SMB growth strategy and revenue outcomes across acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion—translating a deep understanding of Japanese businesses into programs that help advertisers succeed. You will also partner with Sales and global marketing teams to support large-advertiser engagement through events, activations, and coordinated market initiatives. You will bring local insight to global teams and adapt global capabilities to the needs of the Japanese market.



In this role, you will

 - Own SMB revenue and growth goals in Japan, translating market opportunities into a focused strategy and measurable marketing programs.

 - Build acquisition, onboarding, activation, and lifecycle programs that help SMBs launch successfully, see value, and grow their advertising investment.

 - Identify priority customer segments, verticals, and growth opportunities through customer insight, market analysis, and experimentation.

 - Recruit, engage, and grow SMB-focused agencies and partners through education, enablement, co-marketing, and scalable programs.

 - Build awareness and consideration through locally relevant case studies, webinars, events, and educational content, amplified through influencer marketing, owned channels, and paid media.

 - Partner with Sales to connect marketing programs with customer opportunities and improve handoffs across self-serve and sales-assisted journeys.

 - Coordinate with Sales and global marketing teams on large-advertiser events, activations, and market engagement.

 - Adapt global campaigns and programs for Japan, balancing local customer needs with shared resources and capabilities.

 - Measure commercial impact, test new approaches, and scale programs that improve advertiser acquisition, retention, and revenue.

 - Bring customer and agency feedback to Product, Ads Engineering, and global teams to inform the advertiser experience and future growth opportunities.
   
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you have

 - Experience in digital advertising, growth marketing, or advertiser marketing, with a track record of delivering measurable business growth.

 - Deep understanding of Japan’s advertising market, including SMB needs, agency relationships, and local customer behavior.

 - Experience building and launching programs from scratch, setting priorities in ambiguity, and moving from strategy to hands-on execution.

 - Strong knowledge of self-serve advertising and performance marketing, with experience improving acquisition, activation, retention, or expansion.

 - Experience working with agencies and partners to reach, educate, and grow advertisers.

 - Strong analytical judgment and the ability to connect customer insight, funnel performance, and experimentation to revenue outcomes.

 - A track record of working effectively with Sales, Product, and global or regional marketing teams.

 - Strong communication skills in Japanese and English, with the ability to engage local customers and collaborate across global teams.




Experience that would be especially valuable

 - Experience at an advertising technology platform such as Google, Meta, or a comparable business.

 - Experience taking global programs into Japan and using local insights to improve the broader approach.

title: Android Engineer, Plugin Developer Platform
description:
About the Team

The Plugin Developer Platform team builds the APIs, SDKs, and tools that let people extend ChatGPT and Codex. We work on plugins, connectors, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and interactive apps.

We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work covers plugin creation and publishing, the systems that run plugins across our products, and open standards that developers can build on.


About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Android engineer to bring plugins, connectors, and interactive apps to life on mobile. You’ll build the Android experiences and platform foundations that help developers extend ChatGPT and help users discover and use those capabilities from their devices.

You’ll work across native Android interfaces, developer-facing APIs, and the systems that support extensibility on mobile. You’ll collaborate closely with product, design, and platform engineers, owning features from early exploration through implementation, launch, and iteration.

You’ll also engage directly with developers and partners to understand how their workflows translate to Android. Their experience will inform the interfaces and abstractions you build, the problems you prioritize, and the tradeoffs you make.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.


In this role, you will:

 - Build Android experiences for plugins, connectors, and interactive apps within ChatGPT.

 - Develop reusable Android components and interfaces that support a growing ecosystem of developer-built experiences.

 - Partner with platform engineers to connect native mobile experiences with APIs, SDKs, and backend systems.

 - Work with developers and partners to identify integration challenges and improve the experience of building for mobile.

 - Improve app performance, reliability, architecture, testing, and developer tooling.

 - Own projects from initial requirements through release, measurement, and iteration.
   

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have deep experience building Android applications using Kotlin and modern Android development frameworks.

 - Have shipped consumer-facing mobile products at scale and care deeply about performance, quality, and user experience.

 - Bring a platform mindset and enjoy designing reusable interfaces and abstractions that other developers build on.

 - Enjoy collaborating across engineering, product, and design, and working directly with developers and partners.

 - Are excited about bringing AI-powered tools and extensible experiences to mobile.

 - Thrive in fast-moving environments where you help define both product and technical direction.

title: Account Director, Large Enterprise
description:
About the team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their business. The team is made of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals that work together to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

About the role

Our Sales team has a unique mission to help customers understand the deep impact that highly capable AI models can bring to their business and users. This role is a mixture of technical understanding, vision, partnership, and value-driven strategy.

You’ll be a key driver of opportunities through the entire sales cycle, from pipeline generation to closure. You’ll work with researchers, engineers, and solution strategists to help customers evolve their industry with AI.

This role is based in Sydney, Australia. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you'll:

 - Manage a small number of key accounts, developing and executing strategies for a comprehensive account plan

 - Lead our enterprise prospects’ journeys from consideration to successful deployment

 - Partner with solutions and research engineering to build and execute complex customer programs and projects

 - Own a consumption revenue target

We’re seeking a Legal Contracts Manager to support OpenAI for Government’s growing public sector business. This role will manage a wide range of contracting activities with U.S. federal, state, and local government customers and partners.

title: Internal Communications Lead,  Enterprise & Growth
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity.

Our Communications team supports OpenAI’s mission and goals by clearly and authentically explaining our technology, values, and approach to safely building powerful AI. The Internal Communications team aims to create clarity, trust, and shared understanding that inspires our employees to do their best work. We partner across the company to craft clear, compelling narratives about what’s being built, why it matters, how it aligns to our strategy, and most importantly, how it advances our mission.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced internal communications leader to own the strategy for our Enterprise & Growth portfolio, spanning B2B, Revenue, Partnerships, Marketing, Enterprise Engineering, Ads, Commerce, and Consumer Verticals. These teams are changing how businesses operate, bringing AI into working life, and expanding access to its benefits. This work is central to our mission of ensuring AGI benefits all of humanity: helping people and businesses everywhere put AI to use in ways that improve their lives and livelihoods.

You will have the opportunity to work closely with executives to help employees understand where the business is going, why decisions are being made, and how their work ladders up. You will draw on a deep understanding of the teams you support and leverage strong relationships across the company to shape the communications approach and deliver the writing and programs that bring it to life.

A central part of this role is helping employees understand how our technology reaches people and businesses – and what we learn when they use it. You will bring user and customer experiences into companywide conversations, help employees understand the products and capabilities we’re building for businesses and the problems they solve, and help leaders communicate through rapid growth and change.

We’re looking for someone with sharp editorial instincts, boundless creative ambition, and the sound judgment to handle sensitive, confidential, and consequential work with care. You should be equally comfortable setting the communications direction, writing an executive message that addresses what’s on employees’ minds directly and transparently, and hosting a live conversation that invites candid questions and open discussion.

OpenAI is a unique and fast-moving working environment. Priorities can shift quickly, and important work often begins before every detail is settled. You will often need to get up to speed on unfamiliar topics, recommend a path with incomplete information, and adjust as decisions evolve. We’re looking for a pro who takes initiative, understands what matters to employees, and anticipates tough questions and pain points early enough to help leaders address them.

This role can be based in San Francisco or New York City. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Set and deliver the communications strategy for Enterprise & Growth. Understand the portfolio’s priorities, identify where communications can make a difference, and lead programs from initial recommendation through execution and evaluation.

 - Advise senior leaders and shape their communications. Develop leadership updates, narratives, and presentations. Offer clear recommendations on framing, timing, and delivery, holding a high bar for accuracy, clarity, and transparency with employees.

 - Guide communications through complex and sensitive changes. Develop plans for leadership transitions, organizational changes, and evolving business priorities. Work with People, Legal, External Comms, and XFN partners to explain decisions, prepare leadership, and address questions employees are likely to have.

 - Lead company-wide user and customer storytelling. Build programs that show how people and organizations use our technology, how it benefits them, and what employees can learn from their experiences. Develop creative formats that bring these stories to life, encourage engagement, and spark new ideas for what we could build next.

 - Bring employee perspectives into communications decisions. Synthesize questions and feedback from Slack, leadership forums, and other channels. Help leaders understand where employees need more context, recommend responses, and assess whether communications are improving understanding, morale, and trust.

 - Keep work moving as priorities change. Move quickly, adapt as new information comes in, and keep everyone involved informed about decisions and next steps. Respond to feedback, adjust course without losing momentum, and bring a constructive, collaborative attitude to challenging moments.

 - Strengthen the broader Internal Communications function. Contribute to shared priorities, provide thoughtful ideas and feedback, and turn successful approaches into practices others can use.




YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 10+ years of relevant experience in internal or executive communications, marketing communications, operations, or a related field, with demonstrated ownership of complex communications programs. People Management experience (1-2 years minimum) is required.

 - Experience advising senior leaders. You have built trust through preparation, discretion, and thoughtful and strategic recommendations, and can navigate disagreement with confidence and utmost respect.

 - Excellent writing and editorial judgment. You can explain business strategy and complicated decisions clearly, adapt to different leadership voices, and identify the details that make a message trustworthy and credible. You can produce strong work on a short timeline and incorporate detailed feedback without losing the purpose/“the why” of the message.

 - Curiosity about how businesses grow and how people use technology. You can connect commercial priorities, product developments, and customer experiences to our mission and the questions and themes employees care about.

 - Strong program leadership, ownership, and adaptability. You bring structure to ambiguous work and carry it through with limited direction. You can move between strategic planning and hands-on execution, learn an unfamiliar part of the business quickly, and revise your approach when new information changes the picture.

 - Sound judgment and resilience under pressure. You stay constructive, collaborative, and solutions-oriented through compressed timelines, candid feedback, and changes in direction. title: Deployment Lead, FDE - SF
description:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.



About the Role

You will define how OpenAI delivers complex systems to customers. You will own how they are built, shipped, and adopted. You’ll translate business outcomes into a technical plan, run day-to-day execution across FDEs, Researchers, and Customer Engineers, and partner with customer teams to ensure delivery supports their goals.

You will own delivery end-to-end: embedding with customers to map workflows and success criteria, ensuring components ship on time, and leading readiness and change management for adoption. You’ll track progress, manage dependencies, make sequencing decisions, and drive 0→1 prototypes through MVP and scale. You will also share field insights with Product and Research to guide roadmap and priorities.

Success will be measured first and foremost by impact - deployments that deliver measurable value against customer goals, drive adoption, and become critical to their workflows. Additional measures of success include delivery reliability (milestones hit, low reopen/churn), operating leverage (patterns reused across deployments), judgment under pressure, and product impact (field signal that shifts roadmaps/architectures).

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. Success requires deep technical project management expertise, extreme ownership of outcomes, and an ability to immerse in customer workflows and partner with customer teams to solve complex engineering problems at pace.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.



In this role, you will:

 - Own the technical delivery plan for multiple interdependent work streams. Translate business objectives into a roadmap with milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

 - Run day-to-day engineering execution. Track and drive delivery across OpenAI FDE and customer teams. Keep progress unblocked and sequenced. Make real-time trade-offs on scope and priority to protect the critical path.

 - Embed with customer teams to land production deployments and drive adoption. Map workflows, shape tools/integrations, and translate requirements into a delivery plan. Lead onboarding, adoption, and change management.

 - Partner with Product and Research so platform components and research work streams land in time to support deployment goals.

 - Codify solution patterns and evals. Extract reusable patterns and package field signals to improve product and models.

 - Own value cases and ROI. Set impact hypotheses, baselines, and KPIs; run pre-/post-deployment measurement and report to exec sponsors.

 - Shape how we engage Financial Services customers


You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 7+ years of customer‑facing technical delivery leadership 

 - Track record of successfully leading large, complex, high-stakes customer engagements where customer outcomes depended on tight coordination and fast decision making, ideally involving AI.

 - Excel in high ambiguity environments. Know how to simplify complex and dynamic work.

 - Move fluidly between system level understanding and execution level detail; can dive into customer workflows/data, map constraints, sketch architectures and move ambiguous problems to shipped systems.

 - Think strategically and pattern-match. Able to step back from execution detail, recognise broader trends across deployments, and connect customer needs to scalable, reusable solutions.

 - Have strong technical fluency and sharp sequencing instincts. Confident discussing technical details, pressure-testing architectures, and making trade-offs.

 - Have shipped AI/LLM systems. You understand solution patterns, integration basics, and production pitfalls.

title: Strategy and Operations, OpenAI for Government
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The OpenAI for Government team is a dynamic, mission-driven group leveraging frontier AI to transform how governments achieve their missions. Our team works to empower public servants with secure, compliant AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise in custom configurations) and mission-aligned deployments that meet government technical requirements with strong reliability and safety.

As part of the OpenAI for Government team you will work across governments and public institutions, helping to accelerate adoption through hands-on support, tailored training, and early insights—so civil servants can spend less time on red tape and more on meaningful work. If you're passionate about responsibly deploying frontier AI to uplift public institutions and transform how the government serves the American people, we want you on our team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced strategy and business operations professional to help OpenAI for Government decide where to grow and how to build the capabilities needed to serve government customers. You will shepherd ambiguous, complex work from problem definition through execution.  The majority of the role will focus on business strategy and operations, from market and revenue planning to workforce, financial, and secure facility initiatives. You should be skilled at both developing a compelling recommendation and doing the detailed work to make it happen.

This role has four key buckets of responsibilities:

 - First, you will support the growth and maturation of a business operations and revenue strategy function within the OpenAI for Government. You will help OpenAI for Government four vertical leaders develop annual business strategies that define target customers, priority projects, partners, and support needed from other matrixed teams including Technical Success, Engineering, Capture and Proposal, Global Affairs, and Product Policy.

 - You will build and maintain the intelligence picture for our key territories: mission priorities, budget lines and program timelines, incumbents and competitive positions, and the people who actually shape awards.

 - You will act as a thought partner to the business verticals by participating in weekly team discussions to understand the business, test assumptions, and identify risks. You will run quarterly reviews to track progress, reassess goals, and adjust priorities.

 - Second, you will partner with OpenAI’s industrial security team to forecast secure-space needs, plan SCIF buildouts, coordinate personnel access nominations, and track contract-specific security requirements and restrictions.

 - Third, you will support OpenAI’s Government Innovation Network, OpenAI for Government’s advisory board, throughout the entire lifecycle of the program, including advisor outreach and selection, independent-contractor agreements (1099s), conflict reviews, payment, and high-touch onboarding.

 - In partnership with OpenAI for Government’s leadership team, you will help design and run regular advisor meetings, quarterly strategy sessions, and targeted convenings, with clear agendas, materials, and decisions.  You will execute follow-through, and ensure advisor insights are integrated into OpenAI for Government’s strategy.

 - Finally, you will own and drive special projects that do not yet have a clear home. You will define the problem, develop options, build consensus, and lead early execution.

title: Software Engineer, Life Sciences
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. The OpenAI Life Sciences team works at the intersection of advancing frontier life sciences model capabilities and building products to help scientists accelerate their research and leverage the full potential of AI for scientific work.

We’re building platforms that connect model intelligence with practical scientific workflows. Our work covers workflows from next-gen sequencing analysis to designing new drugs, helping scientists run computational workloads as well as access laboratory services. By making these capabilities more accessible and useful, we aim to improve early discovery and support downstream progress in drug development.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for experienced full-stack product engineers with strong backend skills to join our growing Life Sciences team.

This is an individual contributor role with substantial ownership. You’ll help define products, design systems, and ship experiences that connect scientists with AI capabilities and laboratory workflows. You’ll work across the stack, partnering with researchers, scientists, and infrastructure engineers to turn complex needs into reliable, intuitive products.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, product judgment, and experience shipping to large user bases. Life sciences experience is helpful, but you don’t need a scientific background to make a meaningful contribution.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Design backend services, APIs, and integrations that connect users with models, scientific tools, and laboratory services.

 - Create intuitive interfaces that help scientists navigate complex workflows.

 - Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, operation, and iteration.

 - Work with scientific and research partners to identify user needs and prioritize valuable product improvements.

 - Partner with dedicated infrastructure engineers on performance, reliability, and scaling.

 - Make thoughtful engineering decisions that balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals and depth in backend development, alongside the ability to build across the stack.

 - Have shipped and operated products used by large user bases.

 - Bring strong product sense and can translate ambiguous needs into useful software.

 - Work autonomously, make sound technical decisions, and drive projects forward with limited direction.

 - Enjoy hands-on building and taking ownership within a lean team.

 - Are excited about advances in AI and how they could change scientific work.

 - Learn unfamiliar domains quickly and collaborate effectively with scientific and technical partners.


PARTICULARLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE

 - Building AI applications, model-serving integrations, or inference platforms.

 - Developing marketplaces or products that coordinate services and complex workflows.

 - Taking new products from early concepts through launch and adoption.

 - Working with scientific tools, research data, or laboratory systems.

title: Procurement Coordinator
description:
About Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About Role

We’re looking for a Procurement Coordinator to support the day-to-day purchasing and logistics needs of our Robotics organization. You’ll follow up on orders, coordinate domestic and international shipments, work with suppliers and logistics providers, and keep the details organized from purchase request through delivery.

This is an entry-level position for someone who is organized, curious, and eager to take ownership. You don’t need years of procurement experience, but you should be comfortable asking questions, learning quickly, and following through. When an email goes unanswered, you pick up the phone. When a delivery is at risk, you find out why, identify the next step, and keep the right people informed.

You’ll also help improve how we work. We expect you to adopt AI tools and build practical automations that reduce repetitive tasks, improve visibility, and make the supply chain team more effective. This role offers an opportunity to build a foundation in procurement, logistics, and hardware operations.



This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week and up to 10% travel to vendor sites.

In this role you will:

 - Follow up with internal teams to keep purchase requests and PO issuance moving on time, resolve missing information, and confirm that suppliers receive and acknowledge orders.

 - Track open orders through delivery, maintain accurate supplier commitments, and proactively follow up on lead times, shipment dates, and overdue items.

 - Coordinate domestic and international logistics, including scheduling couriers, arranging pickups, booking shipments, tracking deliveries, and resolving shipping exceptions.

 - Prepare and check commercial invoices, packing lists, and other shipping documentation. Work with suppliers, customs brokers, and internal specialists to address customs questions and support timely clearance.

 - Manage day-to-day coordination with third-party logistics providers (3PLs), including receiving, storage, outbound shipments, and resolving inventory or delivery discrepancies.

 - Keep purchasing and logistics records current, communicate clear status updates, and help resolve order discrepancies, returns, and missing delivery documentation.

 - Use AI, spreadsheets, and workflow automation tools to streamline order tracking, follow-up reminders, shipment updates, and routine reporting. Check that the resulting information is accurate and useful.

 - Support the broader supply chain team as priorities shift. Take action on open issues, call suppliers when email isn’t working, and escalate risks early with clear context and proposed next steps.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are starting your career and want to build experience in procurement, logistics, or operations. Relevant experience can come from internships, school projects, part-time work, or other roles where you managed details and followed through.

 - Are highly organized and attentive to detail. You can keep track of multiple orders, deadlines, and follow-ups without losing sight of what matters most.

 - Have a bias for action. You’re comfortable contacting an unfamiliar supplier, asking direct questions, and following up persistently and professionally.

 - Communicate clearly and close the loop. People know what’s happening, what’s blocked, and what you’re doing next.

 - Are comfortable with spreadsheets and learning new systems. You actively experiment with AI tools and can turn a repetitive task into a more reliable workflow.

 - Adapt well to changing priorities, ask for help when needed, and exercise sound judgment about when to act independently and when to escalate.

 - Are curious about robotics, hardware, and how physical goods move through a supply chain. Prior exposure to purchasing systems, shipping, customs documentation, or warehouse operations is helpful but not required.

What success looks like:

Within the first 6 months, you will have:

 - Established reliable tracking for your assigned orders, with current commitments, clear next actions, and timely follow-up.

 - Built effective working relationships with suppliers, couriers, customs brokers, and 3PLs.

 - Become dependable at coordinating routine domestic and international shipments, preparing documentation, and escalating exceptions appropriately.

 - Earned the team’s trust through accurate records, responsive communication, and consistent follow-through.

 - Implemented practical AI or automation improvements that reduce manual work while maintaining accuracy.

title: Technical Accounting Lead, Ads Revenue
description:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance ensures the organization is positioned for long-term success as we pursue our mission. The Revenue team plays a critical role in enabling OpenAI to scale commercial offerings by overseeing billing operations, deal desk, revenue systems, revenue accounting, and controllership. We work cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Go-To-Market, Tax, Legal, and Technical Accounting to support new monetization strategies, improve operational efficiency, and maintain financial integrity as the business grows.

About the Role

This senior leader will own key elements of Ads revenue accounting from technical assessment through operational execution. The role will guide accounting for products, pricing, contracts, incentives, credits, refunds, makegoods, international expansion, and new go-to-market motions. It will establish governance and translate approved accounting positions into launch, billing, data, close, reconciliation, and control requirements. Success requires deep technical revenue expertise, strong business partnership, and the ability to build durable 0-to-1 processes in a fast-changing environment.

Advertising is a critical and growing monetization vector for OpenAI, and this role will help shape the financial foundations that enable Ads to scale responsibly and transparently.

This role can be based in San Francisco or New York City. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will: 

 - Lead technical accounting assessments for Ads products and commercial arrangements, including performance obligations, variable consideration, allocation, principal-versus-agent, collectibility, contract modifications, refunds, incentives, credits, makegoods, and revenue presentation.

 - Own and continuously evolve Ads revenue accounting policies and operating guidance as product behavior, pricing, contracting, incentive programs, and billing models change.

 - Establish governance for new products and accounting decisions, including intake, decision rights, materiality and escalation thresholds, launch approvals, policy versioning, decision logs, and post-launch monitoring.

 - Translate accounting conclusions into clear requirements for product design, contracting, billing, data, estimates, close, reconciliations, controls, and reporting.

 - Own the operating cadence for incentive and makegood accounting, invoice readiness, accruals and reserves, settlements, reconciliations, GL tie-outs, flux analysis, reporting, and control evidence.

 - Partner with Ads Product, Engineering, Data, Finance Engineering, Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, Tax, Billing, and Technical Accounting on launches, enterprise negotiations, and international expansion.

 - Prepare concise technical memos and audit-ready support; align novel or material conclusions with Corporate Technical Accounting and external auditors.

 - Use data, AI, and automation to improve research, monitoring, policy maintenance, issue tracking, documentation, and repeatable Finance workflows with appropriate review controls.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 10+ years of progressive experience in revenue accounting, including direct ownership of complex ASC 606 judgments and operational execution.

 - Demonstrated leadership to independently set direction, prioritize across competing risks, and influence senior cross-functional stakeholders.

 - Experience with digital advertising, adtech, marketplaces, payments, usage-based services, or another high-volume transaction environment.

 - Strong command of variable consideration, principal-versus-agent, contract modifications, incentives and credits, collectibility, estimates, and revenue presentation.

 - Track record building 0-to-1 accounting processes, governance, close mechanisms, reconciliations, and controls that scale.

 - Ability to turn technical conclusions into practical product, contract, billing, data, and operating requirements.

 - Clear, concise written and executive communication, including audit-ready documentation and evidence-based recommendations.

Preferred Qualifications: 

 - Experience supporting global launches, multiple currencies, international contracting entities, intercompany considerations, or localized billing models.

 - Experience applying AI or automation within Finance while maintaining review, validation, and control standards.

 - Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Data, or Finance systems teams.

 - Experience developing or leading high-performing accounting teams or distributed operating groups.

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Growth
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments and other OpenAI products worldwide. We work across the full funnel—from awareness and acquisition through activation, retention, and expansion—using experimentation, data science, machine learning, and product engineering to help more people discover and realize durable value from OpenAI’s products.

Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Finance, Lifecycle, and Growth Marketing. We move quickly, test rigorously, and hold a high bar for measurement, privacy, reliability, and user trust.




ABOUT THIS ROLE: 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to build the models and decision systems that optimize paid marketing investment for ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. You will develop budget allocation and control algorithms that determine where to invest, how quickly to spend, and how to adjust as performance changes.

The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build budget allocation algorithms. Decide how to distribute investment across channels, campaigns, and markets using estimates of marginal returns, while accounting for diminishing returns, uncertainty, and business constraints.

 - Develop spend pacing and adaptive control systems. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior.

 - Model marketing response and user value. Develop forecasts and models of conversion, long-term value, and saturation that help determine where the next dollar can have the greatest impact.

 - Evaluate decisions rigorously. Use simulations, backtesting, and online experiments to test allocation and control policies. Partner with Data Science to measure incrementality and validate whether offline improvements translate into better investment outcomes.

 - Own reliable production systems. Build data pipelines, training and inference workflows, and integrations that turn model outputs into budget decisions. Establish data-quality checks, monitoring, and retraining with thoughtful treatment of privacy and consent.

 - Turn business goals into optimization problems. Partner with Growth Marketing, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance to define objectives and constraints, communicate tradeoffs, and use evidence to improve investment decisions.

 - Help build a diverse and inclusive culture where people feel welcome, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with candor and respect.




You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist, Data Scientist, or in a comparable quantitative engineering role, or an equivalent record of impact.

 - Experience building and operating production ML or quantitative decision systems, from problem formulation and data pipelines through deployment, experimentation, and monitoring.

 - Strong software engineering skills, proficiency in Python and SQL, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks and large-scale data systems.

 - Strong foundations in machine learning and statistics, with experience applying optimization or control methods to decisions under uncertainty.

 - Experience evaluating models or algorithms with noisy, delayed, or incomplete data, and the judgment to balance model quality, causal impact, and operational reliability.

 - The ability to turn ambiguous goals into focused experiments, interpret mixed results, and communicate clear decisions with technical and non-technical partners.

 - A collaborative working style and a commitment to deploying AI responsibly, in service of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

title: Data Program Manager, Science
description:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.

You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

 - Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier.

 - Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.

 - Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms.

 - Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery.

 - Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements.

 - Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop.

 - Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects.

 - Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence.

 - Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations.

 - Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty.

 - Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work.

 - Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction.

 - Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait.

 - Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details.

 - Learn exceptionally quickly, developing your understanding of AI training, evaluation and unfamiliar research areas to become a useful collaborator.

 - We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area.

description:

OpenAI’s Controllership team provides accurate, timely, and decision-useful financial information while building the processes, systems, and controls needed to support a rapidly growing global business. Our Accounting Operations team owns core accounting and close activities and drives improvements that help our finance organization scale.

 

About the Role

We are looking for an Accounting Manager with a strong general accounting foundation and hands-on intercompany experience to join our Accounting Operations team. You will own accounting and close activities across assigned balance sheet and P&L areas, manage intercompany activity for assigned entities, and build efficient, well-controlled processes.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with responsibility for independently managing accounting processes, exercising sound judgment, and reviewing work performed by outsourced partners. You will partner closely with Tax, Treasury, Strategic Finance, and Business Systems to resolve issues, support business growth, and improve how we work.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will: 

 - Own the close for assigned accounting areas, including accruals, prepaids, and other balance sheet and operating expense accounts, ensuring accurate results and timely completion.

 - Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules; resolve accounting issues and maintain clear, audit-ready documentation.

 - Manage intercompany accounting for assigned entities, including cross-charges, reconciliations, and coordination of settlements. Investigate differences and drive timely resolution with counterparties.

 - Support new entities, acquisitions, and business initiatives by establishing accounting workflows and integrating them into the close.

 

You might thrive in this role if you have: 

 - 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, with demonstrated ownership of close processes and experience reviewing others’ work or managing in outsourced support.

 - A strong general accounting foundation and practical knowledge of U.S. GAAP, including accruals, reconciliations, and financial statement analysis.

 - Hands-on intercompany accounting experience, including recording transactions, reconciling balances, and resolving differences across entities.

 - The judgment to independently resolve routine and moderately complex accounting issues, identify risks, and escalate matters with clear recommendations.

 - Experience operating and improving internal controls and supporting financial statement audits.

 - Proficiency with ERP systems and advanced Excel skills; Oracle Fusion experience is preferred, and exposure to Oracle FCCS or another consolidation system is a plus.

 - Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing deadlines and work effectively across teams.

title: Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices
description:
We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.



A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.



You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.



This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.



In This Role, You Will

 - Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

 - Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

 - Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

 - Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

 - Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

 - Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

 - Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

 - Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

 - Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

 - Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

 - Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

 - Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

 - Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

 - Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.



Minimum Qualifications

 - 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

 - Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.



You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

 - A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

 - Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

 - Experience developing one or more of the following:
   
   - HSM firmware or trusted applications
   
   - Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services
   
   - HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware
   
   - PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations
   
   - Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols
   
   - HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems
   
   - Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

 - Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

 - Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

 - Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.

 - Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.

 - The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.

 - Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.



Additional Experience That May Be Helpful

 - Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.

 - Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.

 - Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.

 - Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.

 - Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.

 - Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.

 - Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.

 - Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.

 - Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.

 - Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

title: Software Engineer, Cloud Computer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Browser Use team builds the technology that enables agents to interact with browsers across our products. Our work spans infrastructure, tooling, and user experiences, both on users’ devices and in the cloud. We partner with research to improve our models’ browser-use capabilities and with web standards bodies to shape how agents interact with the web. Our products include ChatGPT for Chrome, the ChatGPT in-app browser, and the cloud computer used in dots and ChatGPT Work.


We see the browser as a universal connector. If we can enable our models to use it effectively, they can do anything. Come help us build the future of browsing!




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a product-oriented engineer to build and scale our cloud computer infrastructure. Our goal is to give every one of our users access to an agent with their own computer in the cloud. Build novel solutions to problems like authentication, user takeover, and enterprise network access. You’ll help own the systems that provision, run, and manage the environments our agents use, making them reliable, responsive, and efficient as demand grows.


This role combines infrastructure depth with close attention to the user experience. You’ll partner with research and engineering teams to bring new computer-use capabilities into production, working across container orchestration, backend services, and product experiences.




IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Build and scale infrastructure for running agent-controlled browsers and computers in the cloud.

 - Develop services for provisioning environments, managing sessions, and coordinating their lifecycle.

 - Improve reliability, performance, resource utilization, and observability across the fleet.

 - Diagnose issues across Linux, containers, networking, and browser execution.

 - Build APIs and tooling that make cloud computers easy for research and product teams to use.

 - Work closely with research to understand emerging requirements and improve how computer use works.

 - Develop authentication, credential management, and network access controls that protect user data and support interactions with websites and services.




YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE

 - Experience leading large-scale backend, platform, or infrastructure projects from ambiguous problem statements to production systems.
